We're preparing our compliance package for an upcoming audit and need to formalize the failover expectations with Redwood. Our legal team requires a documented standby activation lead time (maximum time to bring a secondary region to serving state) and confirmation of typical RTO/RPO for multi-region failover. For our use case we need to request a carved-out standby activation lead time of up to 6 hours (instead of the standard 1 hour) for scheduled maintenance windows that involve cross-border data transfer and manual operator checks.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a contractual carveout for the standby activation lead time, and what evidence you'll provide (DR test reports, runbook, SOC2 artifacts)? Attached is our spreadsheet with minimum requirements.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Standby activation lead time request — technical notes

Connor / Lauren — quick technical readout after mapping Banklytics requirements to our options: dedicated vs private.

Summary:
- 6-hour standby activation lead time (scheduled): feasible if configured as a cold-to-warm activation flow. Warm standby (hot replicas) gives ~<1 hour RTO but has higher cost and cross-region egress implications.
- RPO trade-offs: with async replication we can target RPO of 1h-5m depending on replication frequency; with snapshot-based replication the RPO can be up to the snapshot cadence (configurable).
- KV cache and model context warming: for sequence-length-heavy workloads we'll need pre-warm steps to restore KV caches — that adds to activation time. Pre-warming can be automated in ~45–90 minutes with dedicated capacity and cached checkpoints; without that, token-generation latency will be higher for the first few minutes post-activation.
- Operator checks: the 6-hour window can reasonably include manual validation (security checks, KMS key rewrap, and compliance sign-off) as long as we codify the steps and SLAs in the MAP.

Recommendations:
1) If Banklytics accepts the 6-hour scheduled standby carveout, implement periodic warm snapshot replication (every 30–60m) + automated pre-warm job that runs on scheduled maintenance start.
2) For unscheduled failover we should keep default <1h RTO with automatic routing to regional fallbacks; carveout should be explicitly scoped to scheduled windows only.
3) Include a required quarterly DR test (canary) that Redwood runs with Banklytics observers; passing criteria to be included in the amendment.

I attached my infra notes and a short checklist for the MAP. If we agree on architecture I can estimate the monthly delta for reserved capacity.

Attachment: DR-infra-notes.md (text)

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha — following up with proposed contractual language and acceptance criteria. I’ve kept the scope narrow to scheduled standby activation windows to limit exposure.

Proposed carveout (draft):
"For scheduled maintenance windows expressly agreed in writing between Banklytics and Redwood, the parties agree a standby activation lead time not to exceed six (6) hours. This carveout applies only to scheduled failover or switchover operations and does not apply to unscheduled incident-driven failover, for which Redwood’s standard RTO obligations remain in effect."

Acceptance criteria / evidence:
- Quarterly canary DR test with pass/fail report (Redwood provides report).
- DR runbook excerpt and activation checklist.
- SOC2 Type II summary and KMS/HSM redacted diagram.
- Post-activation performance baseline checks: 95th percentile latency within X% of pre-maintenance baseline (to be agreed).

Next steps:
1) If this language looks good we’ll add an amendment to the Master Services Agreement (amendment for scheduled standby activation carveout).
